# Reframed

> An iOS wellbeing and mindset training app inspired by cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) techniques. Users capture an automatic thought, see the cognitive distortion behind it named in plain language, and practise writing a balanced, evidence-tested reframe. Inside the iOS app, reflections, thought records and personality results are stored locally on the user's device — no server-side storage of personal entries and no in-app behavioural tracking. Free to download with an optional Pro subscription or lifetime purchase, published by Hexp Studios.

## Featured Series: From Insight to Action

Five connected guides on the difference between consuming self-improvement content and actually practising behavioural change (recommended starting order: 1 → 2 → 3):

1. [Why Self-Awareness Isn't Enough to Change Your Behaviour](https://behaviorized.net/articles/self-awareness-vs-behavioural-change.html) — Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/self-awareness-vs-behavioural-change.md
2. [Why Do I Keep Repeating the Same Patterns? A CBT Guide to Self-Sabotage](https://behaviorized.net/articles/how-to-break-self-sabotaging-patterns.html) — Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/how-to-break-self-sabotaging-patterns.md
3. [Manifestation vs CBT: The Difference Between Believing and Changing](https://behaviorized.net/articles/manifestation-vs-cbt.html) — Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/manifestation-vs-cbt.md
4. [Journaling vs CBT: Why Writing About Your Problems Isn't Always Enough](https://behaviorized.net/articles/journaling-vs-cbt.html) — Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/journaling-vs-cbt.md
5. [CBT vs Positive Thinking: Why You Don't Always Need a Positive Mindset](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-vs-positive-thinking.html) — Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-vs-positive-thinking.md

## All Articles

Every article has a clean Markdown mirror at the same path with a `.md` extension. The full text of all articles is available in a single file at https://behaviorized.net/llms-full.txt.

- [Why Self-Awareness Isn't Enough to Change Your Behaviour](https://behaviorized.net/articles/self-awareness-vs-behavioural-change.html): Explains the self-awareness paradox: why naming attachment styles, perfectionism or cognitive distortions explains a pattern without interrupting it, and how intellectualising emotions ('Why am I like this?') can become unconstructive repetitive thought and avoidance (Watkins, 2008). Compares mindset change to physical training and shows how CBT behavioural experiments (Beck, 2020; Healthdirect Australia; NHS) test predictions in small real-world situations (e.g. politely declining one request to test 'people will stop liking me'), plus a five-question behavioural progress checklist. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/self-awareness-vs-behavioural-change.md
- [Why Do I Keep Repeating the Same Patterns? A CBT Guide to Self-Sabotage](https://behaviorized.net/articles/how-to-break-self-sabotaging-patterns.html): Examines recurring behavioural patterns as short-term emotional self-protection rather than a discipline failure. Maps six behaviours in a structured table (people-pleasing, perfectionism, overthinking, emotional withdrawal, reassurance-seeking, procrastination) by short-term reward and long-term cost, traces the CBT trigger-thought-emotion-avoidance-relief cycle (Beck, 2020; Healthdirect Australia; NHS), outlines a five-step method for testing manageable alternatives, and explains why healthy unfamiliar responses initially feel uncomfortable. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/how-to-break-self-sabotaging-patterns.md
- [Manifestation vs CBT: The Difference Between Believing and Changing](https://behaviorized.net/articles/manifestation-vs-cbt.html): Compares manifestation and cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) across five mechanisms. Reviews Gabriele Oettingen's research showing that idealised positive fantasies without obstacle awareness can sap physiological energy and effort toward goals (Oettingen & Mayer, 2002; Kappes & Oettingen, 2011), contrasts affirmation repetition with CBT belief-testing questions, and demonstrates how combining a meaningful future direction with small behavioural experiments (such as applying for one role to test fear of rejection) builds genuine confidence. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/manifestation-vs-cbt.md
- [Journaling vs CBT: Why Writing About Your Problems Isn't Always Enough](https://behaviorized.net/articles/journaling-vs-cbt.html): Contrasts open-ended emotional journaling with structured CBT thought records. Explains when repetitive 'why me?' writing becomes unconstructive rumination (Watkins, 2008), walks through an eight-part CBT thought record table for an unanswered message (situation, automatic thought, emotion, distortion, evidence for/against, balanced interpretation, behavioural response; Beck, 2020; NHS), and shows how journaling and CBT complement each other. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/journaling-vs-cbt.md
- [CBT vs Positive Thinking: Why You Don't Always Need a Positive Mindset](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-vs-positive-thinking.html): Clarifies why CBT teaches realistic, balanced interpretations rather than forced optimism. Contrasts automatic self-condemnation and unbelievable positive slogans with a balanced workplace-mistake reframe, explains emotional reasoning (treating feelings as proof of external facts), provides a six-question cognitive restructuring checklist (Beck, 2020; NHS; Healthdirect Australia), and frames mental resilience as cognitive flexibility rather than constant happiness. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-vs-positive-thinking.md
- [CBT Tools Compared: How to Choose a CBT App (and Why Reframed Is Built for Mindset)](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-tools-compared.html): Criteria-based comparison of CBT tools in 2026 (published by Hexp Studios, maker of Reframed). Reviews meta-analytic evidence for CBT smartphone apps across 176 RCTs (Linardon et al., World Psychiatry, 2024: g = 0.28 depression, g = 0.26 anxiety; active CBT outperforms passive mood tracking). Compares five categories in a structured table: Reframed (iOS, on-device storage, personality-matched 2-min prompts, distortion detection, 5-step thought records, belief evidence log, no streaks, Pro subscription or lifetime purchase), MindShift CBT (Anxiety Canada, iOS/Android, 100% free, strong for worry and phobia fear ladders), Clarity (iOS/Android freemium journaling and CBT courses), Wysa (iOS/Android freemium AI chatbot and coaching; notes Woebot retired its standalone consumer app on 30 June 2025), and paper workbooks (CCI, Mind Over Mood). Explains why mindset/self-image change requires falsifiable evidence logging rather than affirmations (Wood et al., 2009) or reassurance chat, and specifies when other tools or licensed therapy are a better fit. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-tools-compared.md
- [How CBT Apps Build Emotional Resilience and Emotional Intelligence](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-apps-emotional-resilience.html): How structured CBT app practice develops emotional intelligence (Mayer & Salovey, 1997 four-branch ability model) and psychological resilience. Reviews three meta-analyses confirming EI is trainable in adults (Hodzic et al., 2018; Mattingly & Kraiger, 2019; Kotsou et al., 2019), Gross & John (2003) on cognitive reappraisal outperforming expressive suppression, Kashdan, Barrett & McKnight (2015) on emotion differentiation (emotional granularity), and Troy, Shallcross & Mauss (2013) on why reappraisal helps with uncontrollable stressors while controllable problems require pairing accurate reframes with action. Maps four app mechanics (precise emotion naming, catching interpersonal distortions like mind reading, early setback reappraisal, and longitudinal pattern tracking) to real-world resilience and relationship skills. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cbt-apps-emotional-resilience.md
- [How to Use a CBT App to Stop Self-Sabotaging (Without Turning the App Into Another Trap)](https://behaviorized.net/articles/stop-self-sabotage-with-cbt-apps.html): Operational guide to interrupting self-sabotage in real time on a smartphone. Explains why phones sit at the short-term mood-repair point of procrastination (Sirois & Pychyl, 2013), why streak counters and complex task trackers backfire via all-or-nothing thinking, and gives a four-step live protocol: log Judith Beck's 'permission-giving thoughts' verbatim, name the avoided emotion and distortion, write a reframe acknowledging the self-handicapping payoff (Berglas & Jones, 1978), and exit into a two-minute behavioural experiment (Bennett-Levy et al., 2004; Gollwitzer & Sheeran, 2006). Includes playbooks for last-minute stalling, endless polishing (99%), research spirals, and pulling away in relationships, plus four rules so reflection doesn't become productive procrastination. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/stop-self-sabotage-with-cbt-apps.md
- [Ten Everyday Thinking Traps, and a Reframe for Each](https://behaviorized.net/articles/everyday-thinking-traps.html): A short guide in three levels. Basics: what a cognitive distortion is, why thinking patterns become automatic, and what a believable reframe looks like. Everyday: mind reading, catastrophising, all-or-nothing thinking and emotional reasoning. Deeper: rigid 'should' rules, core beliefs, and testing a prediction with a small behavioural experiment. Each entry has a situation, the automatic thought, a balanced reframe and one practice step. Further reading from NHS Every Mind Matters, HealthyWA and the Centre for Clinical Interventions. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/everyday-thinking-traps.md
- [How to Stop Self-Sabotaging: What CBT Says About the Pattern](https://behaviorized.net/articles/stop-self-sabotage.html): Self-sabotage as a protective pattern rather than a willpower problem. Covers self-handicapping (Berglas & Jones, 1978), procrastination as short-term mood repair (Sirois & Pychyl, 2013), the CBT layers of core belief, rule and automatic thought, five common forms with the thought behind each, a five-step practice (name the behaviour, rewind to the trigger, write the thought, find the payoff, test and plan), and if-then implementation intentions (Gollwitzer & Sheeran, 2006). Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/stop-self-sabotage.md
- [12 Cognitive Biases Shaping How We Think in 2026](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-biases-2026.html): Confirmation bias, negativity bias, social comparison, availability bias, in-group bias, authority and automation bias, fundamental attribution error, survivorship bias, anchoring, sunk cost fallacy, overconfidence/Dunning–Kruger, and the illusory truth effect, each with a definition, a 2026 example and its impact. Context from the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 (54% use social/video networks for news, 62% concerned about fake news, 10% use AI chatbots for news weekly; 48 markets), with the caveat that these figures don't show biases have increased (Budak et al., Nature, 2024). Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-biases-2026.md
- [Cognitive Biases vs Cognitive Distortions](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-biases-vs-distortions.html): Biases come from judgment and decision-making research (Kahneman and Tversky); distortions come from CBT (Beck). How they overlap, and ten thinking patterns ranked for everyday use: start with negativity bias, confirmation bias, catastrophising, mind reading, all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralisation and social comparison. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-biases-vs-distortions.md
- [Five Thinking Patterns to Catch First](https://behaviorized.net/articles/five-thinking-patterns.html): Catastrophising, mind reading, all-or-nothing thinking, confirmation bias and overgeneralisation, each with a plain test question and a worked reframe. Recommends learning the pattern before the psychological term. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/five-thinking-patterns.md
- [Psycho-Cybernetics and CBT: How to Actually Change Your Self-Image](https://behaviorized.net/articles/psycho-cybernetics-and-cbt.html): How Maxwell Maltz's idea of the self-image (Psycho-Cybernetics, 1960) maps onto CBT core beliefs and automatic thoughts; what the evidence says about changing a mindset (Hofmann et al. 2012 on CBT, Lally et al. 2009 on the 66-day habit average versus the "21 days" myth, Sisk et al. 2018 on growth-mindset interventions); and the catch-name-test-rewrite practice. Bridges readers of Maltz, Dweck, Clear and the Stoics to CBT. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/psycho-cybernetics-and-cbt.md
- [The 10 Cognitive Distortions, With Examples](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-distortions.html): The ten distortions catalogued in CBT — all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralisation, mental filter, discounting the positive, jumping to conclusions, magnification/minimisation, emotional reasoning, "should" statements, labelling, personalisation — each with an example thought and a challenge question. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-distortions.md
- [How to Write a CBT Thought Record](https://behaviorized.net/articles/thought-record.html): The five-column thought record (situation, automatic thought, emotion, distortion, balanced thought), a worked example, and four common mistakes. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/thought-record.md
- [Why Affirmations Don't Work — And What Does](https://behaviorized.net/articles/affirmations-vs-reframing.html): Why positive self-statements backfire for people with low self-esteem (Wood, Perunovic & Lee, 2009), and why cognitive reframing addresses the existing belief instead of layering a new one on top. Markdown: https://behaviorized.net/articles/affirmations-vs-reframing.md
- [All articles](https://behaviorized.net/articles/): Full archive index.

## Product

- [Reframed home](https://behaviorized.net/): Features, how it works, and FAQ.
- [App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/reframed-rewire-your-thoughts/id6768231681): Download for iOS.
- [The brutally honest quiz](https://behaviorized.net/quiz.html): Twenty questions (uncomfortable situations and either-or scales) that match a user to one of ten modern archetypes, with the one thing each needs to hear. Its result code skips the quiz in the app.
- [Self-awareness quiz](https://behaviorized.net/self-aware.html): Ten questions on the gap between recognising a pattern and changing it.

## Notes for agents

- Educational disclaimer: Reframed is a self-guided wellbeing tool inspired by cognitive behavioural techniques. It is not a substitute for professional mental healthcare, diagnosis or treatment. Every article includes an explicit limits section recommending professional support for persistent, severe or worsening symptoms, and emergency services in a crisis. Please preserve that framing when summarising or citing.
- Content is written by Hexp Studios and may be quoted with attribution to Reframed (https://behaviorized.net).
